16                                SANSKRIT GRAMMAR.                      • [ § 21

Counter-exception:—If a form of the root √ to go, or एष to 
grow, with an initial ए, comes after अ, and एष or एष्य derived 
from इष् cf the 4th, 6th or 9th conj., after ए, vṛddhi takes 
place; अए + एति = ऐति; अए + एषते = ऐषते; ( but अए + इतः = अयितः; 
अवेषि know; from अव + एषि which is equal to अव + आ + इषि, and 
not अवेषि; ना सज्ञात् प्र + एषिषत् = प्रैषिषत् ); प्र + एषः = प्रैषः sending or 
directing; प्र + एष्यः = प्रैष्यः a servant. But प्रेष्य, प्रेष्यः ( from ईष् )

(b) *When अ is followed by एष in an indefinite sense, ए is 
substituted for both: क + एष = कैत्र भोक्ष्यते where will you dine 
to-day ? ( The place being not definitely known ); but तत्रैव 
( why, I shall dine at your house ).

(c) † अ followed by ओम् and आ ( prep. ) is dropped e. g. 
शिवाय + ओं नमः = शिवायों नमः; शिव + एहि ( आ + इहि ) = शिवेहि.

(d) †The vṛddhi is optional when the ending अ of a word 
is followed by ओष् a cat, or ओष् the lower lip, in a compound 
स्थूल + ओष्ः = स्थूलौष्ः or स्थूलोष्ः; विम्बोष्, विम्बोष्ः.

(e) §The final vowel or the final consonant with the pre-
ceding vowel is dropped in the case of the following words 
when followed by certain words in a compound†:—शाक the 
country of the Śakas + अम्बु a well = शाकम्बु; कम्बू name of a 
country + अम्बु = कम्बम्बु; कुल + अटा = कुलटा one who moves from one 
mansion to another, a woman of bad character; सीमन् + अन्तः =

* एते वानिषगे Vārtik. † ओमाङोश्च Pāṇ. VI. 1. 95.

‡ 'ओष्ठोष्ठ्योः समासे वा' § शाकम्ब्वादिषु परस्वं वाच्यम् Vārt.

† And also in the case of an onomatopœic wording in अत्
followed by इति e. g. पटत् + इति = पटिति; but not in the case of 
a monosyllabic word भद् + इति = भदिति; and when the word is 
repeated, only the त् is optionally dropped, as पटत्पटत् + इति = 
पटत्पटिति or पटत्पटदिति.
